Oaxacan Tamales

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 8-10 (makes about 20-24 tamales)Prep 2 hoursCook 1 hour 30 minutes

Oaxacan tamales, distinguished by their banana leaf wrapping, offer a unique aroma and moist texture, making them a festive favorite. They are a central dish for Día de la Candelaria (Candlemas) on February 2nd in Mexico, a day when families gather to enjoy tamales, often hosted by whoever found the baby Jesus figurine in the Rosca de Reyes.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900 g) masa harina for tamales (not instant masa for tortillas)
  • 1.5 cups (340 g) lard or vegetable shortening, softened
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 4 cups (960 ml) warm chicken broth, plus more if needed
  • 2 pounds (900 g) pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks
  • 1/2 onion, quartered
  • 3 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • Water to cover pork
  • 8-10 dried Guajillo chiles, stems and seeds removed
  • 3-4 dried Ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
  • 1/2 onion, roughly chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) reserved pork cooking broth
  • Salt to taste for sauce
  • 1 (16-ounce / 450 g) package banana leaves, thawed if frozen, cut into 8x8 inch (20x20 cm) squares

Method

  1. Prepare Pork Filling: Place pork shoulder, 1/2 onion (quartered), 3 cloves garlic, and 1 teaspoon salt in a large pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until pork is very tender. Reserve 1/2 cup (120 ml) of the cooking broth. Shred the cooked pork with two forks.
  2. Prepare Red Chile Sauce: While pork cooks, toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until fragrant (do not burn). Place toasted chiles in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let soak for 20-30 minutes until softened.
  3. Drain the softened chiles, reserving some soaking liquid. Blend the chiles with 1/2 chopped onion, 3 cloves garlic, cumin, oregano, and 1/2 cup (120 ml) reserved pork broth until very smooth. Add a splash of chile soaking liquid if needed to help blend.
  4. Strain the chile sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan to remove any skin or seeds. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt to taste.
  5. Combine the shredded pork with enough red chile sauce to coat it well (you may not use all the sauce). Set aside.
  6. Prepare Banana Leaves: If using banana leaves, gently pass each leaf square over an open flame or hot skillet for a few seconds until pliable. This prevents cracking.
  7. Prepare Masa: In a large bowl or stand mixer with a paddle attachment, beat the softened lard (or shortening) until light and fluffy, about 5 minutes.
  8. In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina, 2 teaspoons salt, and baking powder. Gradually add the masa harina mixture to the beaten lard, alternating with warm chicken broth, mixing until a soft, spreadable dough forms. The masa should be light and fluffy. To test if it's ready, drop a small piece into a glass of cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If not, beat for a few more minutes and retest.
  9. Assemble Tamales: Lay a banana leaf square flat with the smooth side up. Spread about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of masa evenly over the center of the leaf, leaving a border.
  10. Place 1-2 tablespoons of the pork filling in the center of the masa.
  11. Fold one long side of the banana leaf over the filling, then fold the other long side to overlap. Fold up the bottom and top ends to create a neat packet.
  12. Steam Tamales: Place a steamer basket in a large pot with about 2 inches (5 cm) of water, ensuring the water does not touch the basket. Arrange the tamales upright or stacked, but not too tightly, in the steamer.
  13. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover tightly, and steam for 1 to 1.5 hours.
  14. Check for Doneness: Tamales are done when the masa easily separates from the banana leaf. If it sticks, steam for another 15-20 minutes and recheck.
  15. Let the tamales rest for 10-15 minutes after steaming before serving.

Tips

  • For an authentic touch, add a small piece of avocado leaf to each tamale before folding.
  • Cooked tamales can be frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat by steaming for 20-30 minutes or microwaving until hot.
  • Vary the filling with shredded chicken in green salsa (salsa verde) or cheese with jalapeños for different options.
